answer: Cast one ceramic anchor per applicant in the registry foundry, its violet glaze crackling into a pattern no second anchor shares, then lower it onto one numbered mooring block — no block holds two. Resting in a velvet-lined cradle, the anchor is photographed; the next challenge is hashed from that photograph and the holder's key, so no reading unlocks a second anchor. A stolen snapshot fails: no two glazes crack alike. One more identity means one more anchor: $290 and 20 foundry-hours, one anchor per kiln firing, so 4,000 clones cost $1.16 million and 80,000 kiln-hours no wholesaler can sell.
